payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the source background been replaced by a visibly recognizable basketball-court setting?
node.criteria: Compare SOURCE with EDITED: pass if the background in EDITED depicts a recognizable basketball court, evidenced by a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment; fail if the background remains the source setting or is not recognizably a basketball court; unknown if the background cannot be observed.
node.binding: The requested background change must be visibly complete in the edited image.
node.source_quote: Change the background into a basketball court
node.endpoint: The background depicts a recognizable basketball court.
node.necessity: The instruction explicitly requests changing the background into a basketball court. A background that does not depict that setting leaves the requested change incomplete.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a kitchen, while the edited background is dark and mostly featureless. A hoop and basketball appear at the left, and another basketball at the lower right, but no recognizable playing surface with court markings is visible; the background does not clearly depict a basketball-court setting.

response.content: {"text":"The trace identifies real basketball cues (hoop and balls) but overlooks the visible court floor and boundary markings in the edited image; its claim that no playing surface or markings are visible is not supported. Reassess the whole background rather than letting the dark, plain upper area dominate: distinguish a partially visible court from an unchanged kitchen or an unrecognizable setting, and calibrate confidence to that evidence. Keep the completion criterion tied to a recognizable basketball-court background, not merely the presence of basketball equipment. The trace is valid and has no dependency or transport failure, so address visual interpretation rather than execution."}
